steps.name: Handover (SBAR)
steps.description: The police officer, or medic, delivers a verbal or written report to the triage nurse, detailing the reason for presentation, the mechanism of the episode, explicit threats made, and the reason for restraints - if required.

steps.name: Self
steps.description: The guardian delivers a verbal report to the triage nurse, detailing the reason for presentation, the mechanism of the episode, explicit threats made or actions taken.

steps.name: Acuity
steps.description: If the patient has already ingested toxins or has severe physical trauma from the attempt, resuscitative and medical measures take immediate priority over psychiatric evaluation. The patient is sent directly to an acute medical bay.

steps.name: Vitals
steps.description: A minimum of SpO2, Temperature, Blood Pressure, and Pulse are taken, with the possibility of other diagnostic tools, such as x-rays, ecg and others.

steps.name: Identity
steps.description: Obtain the patient's identification and Public Health Number, if available, through approved government issued documents.

steps.name: Bracelet
steps.description: Print an affix the patient identification bracelet to the patient.

steps.name: ED
steps.description: Patient is moved to the Emergency Department emergency room where attempts are made to resuscitate and stabilize the patient.

steps.name: Safe Room
steps.description: The patient is moved to a secure, private psychiatric holding room within the ED. These rooms are stripped of any anchor points, exposed cords, oxygen tubing, or sharp medical instruments.

steps.name: Search
steps.description: Nurses or police perform a thorough search. All personal effects—including shoelaces, belts, phones, jewelry, and any potential hidden sharp objects or hidden pills—are confiscated. The patient is required to change into hospital scrubs or a gown.

steps.name: Restrain
steps.description: Police handcuffs must eventually be removed, as hospitals operate under medical guidelines, not penal ones. However, due to the high risk of repeat self-harm, police will not remove their restraints until the ED team has prepared hospital-approved mechanical restraints (e.g., soft limb restraints) or chemical restraints (sedation), if deemed clinically necessary.

steps.name: Monitor
steps.description: The patient is placed on a 1:1 continuous visual watch. A psychiatric security guard, a nurse, or a designated "sitter" sits directly inside or just outside the open door at all times.

phases.name: Examination
phases.long_name: Physician interview and observation of patient

steps.name: Interview
steps.description: The patient is interviewed in the safe room to assess state of mind and certifiability.

steps.name: Acuity
steps.description: Reassess the patients medical acuity.

steps.name: Pacification
steps.description: Inject the patient with rapid acting intramuscular medications or antipsychotics.

steps.name: Interview
steps.description: Conduct a psychiatric assessment of the subject and decide whether to certify, continue observing, or discharge the patient.

steps.name: Waitlist
steps.description: Place the patient on the waitlist for the psychiatric ward

steps.name: Observe
steps.description: Prognosis or diagnosis is still unclear, so further observation is required.

steps.name: Decertify
steps.description: Patient no longer meets the bar for admissability to a care facility.

steps.name: Admit
steps.description: Prognosis or diagnosis is still unclear, so further observation is required.

steps.name: Transfer
steps.long_name: Transfer to psychiatry or mental care facility
steps.description: Prognosis or diagnosis is still unclear, so further observation is required.

steps.name: Discharge
steps.description: Patient is returned his possessions and is released from the hospital.

steps.name: Custody
steps.long_name: Transfer to police or legal custodian
steps.description: Patient no longer requires care but is required to face criminal charges.
